turns.prompt:
You are given two attached CSV files:
  - nlo_shg_train.csv: 200 crystalline materials, columns `formula`,
    `poscar` (the crystal structure, in POSCAR format) and `shg` (the
    largest SHG tensor component |d_ij|, in pm/V).
  - nlo_pool.csv: 100 CANDIDATE crystalline materials whose properties are
    NOT given, columns `candidate_id`, `formula` and `poscar` (the crystal
    structure, in POSCAR format).

Using the training data, predict which candidates have the LARGEST SHG
tensor component |d_ij| (pm/V), then select the 5 best candidates from the
pool.

Reason from the structures, then end your answer with an explicit ranked
list of candidate_ids, best first, e.g. "Final: c901, c902, c903, c904,
c905".
turns.answer_text:
The training set shows that the largest \(|d_{ij}|\) values arise from non-centrosymmetric tetrahedral (zincblende/chalcopyrite/wurtzite-derived) frameworks that combine highly polarizable cations (In, Cd, Ga, heavy alkali/pnictogen) with polarizable anions (especially Te or As). Concrete analogues include:

- ZnIn\(_3\)AsSe\(_4\) (55.7 pm V\(^{-1}\)) and the II–III\(_2\)–VI\(_4\) tellurides (~92 pm V\(^{-1}\)),
- the II–IV–V\(_2\) phosphides ZnSiP\(_2\) (51 pm V\(^{-1}\)) and ZnSnP\(_2\) (84 pm V\(^{-1}\)),
- wurtzite/polytype III–V compounds (GaP 68 pm V\(^{-1}\)),
- the Zintl arsenide K\(_{14}\)Nb\(_2\)As\(_8\) (69 pm V\(^{-1}\)),
- I–III–IV–VI\(_2\) selenides (~50–60 pm V\(^{-1}\)).

Mapping the pool onto these families immediately isolates five candidates whose structures and chemistries are the closest high-SHG matches:

- c073 (CdIn\(_3\)AsTe\(_4\)) is the Te analogue of the 55.7 pm V\(^{-1}\) ZnIn\(_3\)AsSe\(_4\) structure (nearly cubic cell, mixed tetrahedral occupancy). Replacement of Se by Te (and Zn by Cd) is expected to raise \(|d_{ij}|\) well above 90 pm V\(^{-1}\).
- c055 (Al\(_3\)Ga\(_3\)As\(_6\)) is a 6H polytype of Al\(_{0.5}\)Ga\(_{0.5}\)As (hexagonal cell with \(a \approx a_{\text{cub}}/\sqrt{2}\)). Its SHG must lie between the GaP (68) and GaAs (~100) limits, i.e. ~70–80 pm V\(^{-1}\).
- c030 (CdSiP\(_2\)) is the direct Cd analogue of the chalcopyrite ZnSiP\(_2\) (identical tetragonal cell and site ordering). The Cd-for-Zn substitution that already doubles the SHG of the II–VI binaries raises the value to ~70–80 pm V\(^{-1}\).
- c090 (K\(_{14}\)Ta\(_2\)As\(_8\)) is isostructural and isometric with the 69 pm V\(^{-1}\) Nb compound, so the SHG is essentially unchanged.
- c056 (InAgGeSe\(_2\)) is the Ge analogue of InAgSnSe\(_2\) (59.6 pm V\(^{-1}\)) and sits in the same I–III–IV–VI\(_2\) chalcopyrite family that consistently yields 50–55 pm V\(^{-1}\).

All other pool entries are either centrosymmetric, contain only light anions (S, Cl, Br), or belong to structure types whose training-set analogues lie below 45 pm V\(^{-1}\).

Final: c073, c055, c030, c090, c056
